caption: The entrance sign for Castlepark, framed by a beautiful mature Sycamore in full May leaf. The dappled shade under the canopy is exactly the kind of habitat we want to lean into around our estate boundaries (May 2026)

The wildflower border curving along the corner of the Castlepark wall, under the mature Sycamore canopy. Dandelions, Cow Parsley and other native wildflowers come up naturally each spring from the seed bank, and we keep the bark mulch topped up to give the new seedlings a head start. A simple, low-cost piece of biodiversity work that produces real colour and pollinator value (May 2026)

A pair of mature Sycamores behind the pebble-dash boundary wall at Castlepark. Mature trees inside an estate boundary do enormous biodiversity work — habitat for birds, insects, lichens and bats — and they soften the streetscape no end (May 2026)

A tall multi-stemmed Silver Birch on the roadside opposite Castlepark. Birch is a fantastic native tree for biodiversity (over 300 insect species feed on it) and the white papery bark is a stand-out feature any time of year (May 2026)

The lawn at the left-hand side of the Castlepark entrance, freshly mown and edged with mature trees and shrubs along the boundary wall. A tidy, well-kept estate green that frames the entrance nicely (May 2026)
